prompt:
Create ONE native editable SVG contact sheet containing NINE finished fantasy card artwork illustrations. This is a production packing experiment: every scene must be individually usable and share the same visual style. Canvas exactly 1440 by 1008; viewBox="0 0 1440 1008". Grid is exactly THREE columns and THREE rows, with NO gutters and NO labels. Each cell is exactly 480 by 336 (10:7). Column order left to right is Metallicize, Ghostly Armor, Sentinel. Row order top to bottom is regular, upgraded, future second upgrade. No scene may cross a cell boundary.

STRUCTURE: make each cell a separate top-level SVG group with the corresponding id: metallicize-base, ghostlyArmor-base, sentinel-base, metallicize-upgraded, ghostlyArmor-upgraded, sentinel-upgraded, metallicize-future, ghostlyArmor-future, sentinel-future. Give every group its own dark background rectangle filling its exact 480 by 336 cell. All paths for a cell belong to that cell's group, using a translation if convenient. Do not use a single background across the entire sheet. Static vector paths and simple shapes only; no embedded raster, scripts, fonts, external resources, animation or visible text. Keep construction economical and separable; no unnecessary decoration.

SHARED ART DIRECTION: restrained engraved fantasy print; connected angular and curved material planes, three broad value groups, sparse form-following cuts. Strong readable contours at 160 by 112 and 80 by 56. Dark ink #172928 background, shadow #4c5b55, steel #a9b4aa, warm ivory #dfd0b0, selective muted copper #b97c5e, spectral teal #80a69c. Light from upper left. Consistent scale, crop and margins: each subject fills roughly 75 percent of its scene, with quiet background and at least 24 pixels of clear space around the silhouette. No card frame, border, text, number, logo, watermark, photorealism, plastic gloss, bright gradients, tiny clutter or repetitive engraving. Build broad sculptural planes first; fine detail is subordinate. Different cards need unmistakably different subjects, and upgrades must alter gesture or supporting structures rather than merely recolor the regular illustration.

LEFT COLUMN — METALLICIZE, identity = hardening a single bent forearm into fitted steel. The arm cuts diagonally upward; no floating helmet or full warrior. Top regular: a bent gauntleted forearm with three broad overlapping plates closing over its outer surface, an open elbow silhouette and very restrained copper seams. Middle upgraded: same arm family but a stronger braced fist and an interlocked second layer of broad plates extending toward the elbow, clear change in pose and contour. Bottom future second upgrade: a forceful forward bracing gesture, fitted articulated steel from fist to elbow, one distinctive large copper locking clasp and stronger connected shoulderward structure; preserve the readable single-arm identity, do not become a giant pile of spikes. Each tier should be more resolved and protective, not just brighter or more detailed.

CENTER COLUMN — GHOSTLY ARMOR, identity = an EMPTY spectral suit with large hollow negative space. No head, helmet, skull, face or living body. Top regular: an empty breastplate, connected asymmetric pauldrons and tapered arm guards floating in a calm diagonal sweep, a visibly hollow neckline and open lower hem, restrained vapor through one gap. Middle upgraded: an alert turning gesture, one shoulder leading and one arm-guard sweeping across the chest opening, a larger clean hollow passage and two broad spectral ribbons; the armor remains visibly empty. Bottom future second upgrade: a wider protective mantle shape and opened bracing arms forming a sheltering arch around a large hollow torso, a few connected trailing plates and one quiet teal sweep; no tiny floating shards. Preserve connected anatomy of armor without filling its empty center.

RIGHT COLUMN — SENTINEL, identity = an armored watchman with planted weight behind a tall asymmetric shield. Top regular: compact low guarding stance, one bent knee and one braced rear foot, worn tall shield dominant, a small copper reserve visible at its edge. Middle upgraded: the watchman shifts into a firm forward brace, shield planted with a clear ground contact and a distinct angled upper rim, visible bent supporting arm and a slightly opened reserve aperture. Bottom future second upgrade: an assertive grounded bulwark pose, broad shield angled to protect a clear pocket of space, stronger but restrained copper reserve inside a protected recess and a connected sweeping cloth tail. Each version has clear feet, shield thickness and weight; no floating body, generic helmet emblem, explosions or gratuitous spikes.

Treat this as one coherent art set with nine carefully composed scenes, not a comic, not nine repeated icons. The two upgrade rows are different finished illustrations of the same three identities. Keep all nine scenes useful when extracted as individual 10:7 card-window images.
